newsitem.title: UK: Argentina sets first euro fungible bond for Latam.
newsitem.headline: Argentina sets first euro fungible bond for Latam.

text.p: Argentina on Wednesday launched the first Eurobond from Latin America that will be fungible with another of its outstanding deals once the single European currency comes into effect.
Syndicate manager at Creditanstalt Bankverein in Vienna said a clause would be included in the EMTN programme stating the deals would merge when the euro is implemented.
"This is the first euro-fungible deal for a Latin American country and we have been very pleased with the response" he said.
The one billion Austrian shilling bond is fungible with an outstanding seven-year mark bond launched in February. Both deals pay the same seven percent coupon and mature in March 2004.
The CABV syndicate manager said the bonds were targeted at retail investors.
Argentina is rated B1 by Moody's Investors Service and recently upgraded to BB by Standard and Poor's Corp.

Argentina is also planning to launch a 500 billion lire seven-year bond, an official at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell recently told Reuters. He said the country was also eyeing the dollar and mark sectors.
Meanwhile Brazil is planning the first "parallel bond" for a Latin American borrower.
The issue is likely to be launched in one or more core European currencies with a redenomination clause into euros if European Economic and Monetary Union goes ahead.
